text:
alex: Quick heads-up — I ran a perf sweep on the kernel picker for causal workloads and found a weird cliff at head_dim % 16 != 0. v3 used to be our sweet path but for head_dim=30 it keeps picking v2 fallback and it's 2.8x slower. logs attached below.

jasmin: ugh, seen similar on a customer model a month ago. is this only on Ampere or also on Hopper? :thinking_face: 

alex: repro is on A100 (Ampere) but I reproduced on H100 too. seems tied to our causal padding heuristic + the head packing logic.

raj: can you paste the kernel selection trace? curious which rule triggers the fallback.

alex: sure — snippet from local debug run: 
```
[KernelPicker] model=llama-13b seq=1024 head_dim=30 n_heads=30 causal=true
-> candidate kernels: flash_v3, sdpa_v3_causal, sdpa_v2_causal, flash_v2
-> cost_estimates: flash_v3=9.2, sdpa_v3_causal=8.9, sdpa_v2_causal=8.1, flash_v2=7.3
-> compatibility_checks:
   flash_v3: FAIL (kvcache layout misalign, head_dim % 8 != 0)
   sdpa_v3_causal: FAIL (tiling requires head multiple of 32)
   sdpa_v2_causal: PASS
-> selected: sdpa_v2_causal (latency 7.3ms)
```
alex: note the cost_estimates are optimistic for v3 variants because they assume vectorized head packing; but compatibility knocks them out.

kyle: is the 'kvcache layout misalign' check strict? could we relax it to allow an inefficient path (extra padding) rather than rejecting v3 entirely?

jasmin: we do that for non-causal (pad to 32) but causal has strict no-pad rule to keep latency predictable. maybe that's too strict.

raj: If we allow a one-time pad for KV layout and then adjust decoding to ignore pad, we might keep v3. But memory blowup for long context? need to quantify.

perf-bot: benchmark run finished: 
- config: seq=1024 hd=30 nheads=30 causal=true
- sdpa_v2_causal: p50=7.3ms p95=9.1ms
- flash_v3 (forced via patch): p50=3.2ms p95=4.6ms
- note: forced flash_v3 used 24% more GPU memory due to padding.

alex: forcing flash_v3 shows the huge win. but allocator fragmentation + padding cost might bite production for larger batches. still, 3.2ms vs 7.3ms is huge.

kyle: alternative: change autotuner to prefer kernels that require minor padding if the win outweighs memory delta. Need a knob: max_pad_ratio (e.g., 0.3) and memory_safety_margin.

jasmin: agree. also the head_dim=30 case is common for some community models. we should add a special-case bucketization in the picker: treat head_dim in [17..32] as packable -> prefer v3 with pad. That'd avoid churn.

raj: we need microbenchmarks across seq lengths. maybe at seq<=64 the overhead of pad is no longer justified. put a seq threshold too.

alex: I've sketched a fix: 1) compute pad_bytes = (pack_alignment - (head_dim % pack_alignment)) % pack_alignment 2) pad_ratio = pad_bytes * head_dim / (head_dim * seq) ?? (will refine) 3) if pad_ratio < max_pad_ratio && est_latency_gain > threshold -> allow v3. I can open a PR.

jasmin: please include a perf regression test and a metric for worst-case memory delta per-GPU. also add feature-flag to revert.

perf-bot: created benchmark job: r=alex/allow-pad-v3, queue=high, expires=72h.

kyle: one more thought — causal vs non-causal tile constraints differ because of how we stream KV. maybe we can implement streaming-friendly padding that doesn't allocate per-step. could be a bigger change but worth exploring.

alex: good notes. I'll open PR with two changes: picker heuristic bailout tweak + unit perf job + docs. starting with small feature-flagged change.

raj: thanks alex — please tag me on the PR and put the benchmark link. :+1:

jasmin: nailing this will knock down a bunch of customer regressions. :tada:
